title: Cloud adoption case
prompt: A rural college wants to move its course documents from USB drives to a cloud service. Explain three benefits, three risks, two controls and distinguish SaaS from local software. End with a justified recommendation.
hint: Group your response by benefits, risks, controls and recommendation. Tie each point to the college.
check: Check for three distinct benefits and risks, two specific controls and a justified recommendation. Explain how hosted applications differ from locally installed software.

title: Computing vocabulary
prompt: Define: dedicated device, portable device, cloud storage, file compression and software update. Give a practical example for each.
hint: For each term, write what it does and one place you would use it.
check: Each of the five entries should have its own definition and a plausible real-life example.

title: Email professionalism
prompt: Rewrite this unsuitable email as a professional message to a college administrator: 'HEY!!! u lost my marks AGAIN send them NOW!!!'. Supply a subject, greeting, clear request, identifying information without private ID, closing and explain three email safety rules.
hint: Plan the subject, purpose, identifying context and sign-off before drafting.
check: Check that your subject makes the request clear. Include the course or assessment details needed to locate the result, a respectful request, a closing and three specific safety habits.

title: Communication comparison
prompt: Compare FTP and VoIP in purpose and give a workplace use for each. Explain two benefits and two limitations of electronic communication.
hint: Give both tools the same comparison headings.
check: FTP is for file transfer. VoIP carries voice over an IP network. Compare their uses and support your discussion with concrete benefits and limitations.

title: Data-to-decision exercise
prompt: A campus records attendance as 28, 31, 29, 32, 30. Calculate the mean; explain data versus information; propose a verification check and validation rule; decompose an attendance-report workflow into four steps.
hint: Separate the source-matching check from the allowed-value rule.
check: The mean is 30. Raw attendance counts become information when interpreted. Verification compares values to the source. Validation applies a rule such as accepting whole numbers within room capacity.

title: Logic statements
prompt: For each statement indicate True/False and justify briefly: (a) Verification checks whether copied data matches a source. (b) Validation guarantees a fact is true. (c) Decomposition breaks problems into parts. (d) Abstraction focuses on relevant detail. (e) Raw data is always a decision.
hint: Look carefully at absolute language such as “guarantees” and “always”.
check: Compare your decisions with True, False, True, True, False. Explain each verdict, especially why a valid value can still be inaccurate.

title: Digital citizenship audit
prompt: A student posts a class list publicly, reuses passwords and forwards a suspicious link. Identify three risks, propose four corrective actions, explain digital footprint and name two accessibility accommodations.
hint: Pair each observed action with a risk and a practical control.
check: Check for privacy, account security and suspicious-link exposure. Tie the controls to the risks and explain how online activity leaves a lasting record.

title: Social-media classification
prompt: Give an example and appropriate educational use for each: social networking, photo sharing, video sharing, blogging and interactive community platform. Explain why categories can overlap.
hint: Name the platform, the educational task and a case where its function overlaps.
check: Check that all five platform categories have a suitable example and clear educational use. A video-sharing platform may also host community discussions.

title: Safety training notebook
prompt: Create notebook Campus Safety; sections Orientation and Incidents; pages Fire Procedure and Incident Log. Add a formatted 3-column table (Hazard, Action, Contact), three entries, a dated checklist, a labelled sketch made with drawing tools, and an embedded screenshot of a locally created notice. Print or export evidence.
hint: Create the notebook structure first, then add content, drawing and output evidence.
check: Check both sections and both pages, the three-column table, three entries, a dated checklist, an editable drawing, a screenshot and readable evidence.

title: Organise research notes
prompt: Create notebook Student Support, section Services, pages Library and Counselling. Add an introductory paragraph and three bullets per page. Add a tag to one important task, move a paragraph between pages and show the final page hierarchy in evidence.
hint: Use the notebook sidebar to check the final hierarchy before exporting evidence.
check: Check the final page hierarchy, three bullets per page, the tagged task, the relocated paragraph and evidence of the finished structure.

title: Formal circular
prompt: Create a circular for the Ndlovu Training Centre about a career fair on 12 February 2027. Include a 3-row programme table: Registration 09:00; Employer talks 10:00; CV clinic 11:30. Use A4 portrait, 2.54 cm margins, 12 pt body, a 16 pt centred heading, a right tab stop for date, page number and header with candidate number and W01.
hint: Set page geometry before formatting the title and programme.
check: In print preview, check A4 portrait, page boundaries, the three programme rows, the aligned date, heading styles, header and page number.

title: Edit and proofread
prompt: Create a two-page information sheet on safe online job applications (minimum 230 words). Include two section headings, a five-item numbered list, a footnote defining 'phishing', one landscape section for a comparison table, a page break and a footer. Use Find and Replace to change all occurrences of 'applicant' to 'candidate'.
hint: Use section breaks around the landscape page. Preview the pages before saving.
check: Check both orientations in preview. Confirm the numbered list, footnote, separate page break, footer and the updated wording.

title: Mail merge and labels
prompt: Create recipient data with fields Name, Surname, Town, Session for: Naledi Molefe/Bloemfontein/Morning; Peter Dube/Klerksdorp/Afternoon; Amina Patel/Polokwane/Morning; Zola Maseko/Mahikeng/Afternoon. Draft an invitation to a digital skills workshop on 18 May 2027 with a personalised greeting and session. Merge four letters and create a matching set of four address labels.
hint: Check the recipient table and preview each record before finishing the merge.
check: Preview four letters and four labels. Each letter should pull the correct personalised greeting and session from the recipient data.

title: Advanced table and document layout
prompt: Create a landscape report containing a five-column equipment inventory with four rows. Items: Laptop 6 at R7200; Printer 2 at R2500; Router 3 at R980; Projector 1 at R8400. Include calculated total cost as text after working it out, table caption, borders, shading, row sorting by item and a watermark reading TRAINING COPY.
hint: Keep numeric amounts consistent and sort entire rows together.
check: Grand total R59,540. Compare each quantity × unit cost, then check row sorting, caption, borders, shading, watermark and landscape preview.

title: Fees and discount analysis
prompt: Enter columns Learner, Course, Fee, Paid, Balance, Status. Records: Neo/Office/R1800/R900; Musa/IT/R2400/R2400; Priya/Office/R1800/R1800; Thuli/IT/R2400/R1200; Zola/Office/R1800/R600. Calculate Balance and IF Status = SETTLED when Balance=0 otherwise OUTSTANDING. Summarise total fees, total paid, outstanding balance and count of settled accounts.
hint: Test your IF formula on one fully paid learner before filling down.
check: Total fees R10,200, total paid R6,900, amount outstanding R3,300 and two settled learners. Check that the status column uses a formula.
alignment: 2022 Q9–10; 2023 Q9; 2024/2025 Q9 and later spreadsheet tasks; 2020 Section C

title: Commission with absolute reference
prompt: Create columns Agent, Sales, Commission, Net. Rows: Lindi 12500, Omar 18200, Zanele 9600, Farai 21400. Put commission rate 7.5% in H2. Use an absolute reference to calculate Commission, then Net=Sales-Commission. Add totals and currency formatting.
hint: Keep the commission rate fixed when copying formulas down.
check: Total commission R4,627.50. Excel should retain the same rate-cell address when the formula is copied. Check total sales of R61,700 and net of R57,072.50.
alignment: 2022 Q9–10; 2023 Q9; 2024/2025 Q9 and later spreadsheet tasks; 2020 Section C

title: Criteria functions and chart
prompt: Enter department requests: Library 24; Finance 18; IT 36; Student Affairs 22; Security 10. Compute grand total, share of each department, count of departments with requests >=20 and the second-largest value. Create a column chart with a meaningful title and axis labels.
hint: Keep the grand total fixed in the percentage formula.
check: Grand total 110, three departments at or above 20 and second largest 24. Shares should total 100% before rounding. Inspect the chart labels.
alignment: 2022 Q9–10; 2023 Q9; 2024/2025 Q9 and later spreadsheet tasks; 2020 Section C

title: Lookup and validation
prompt: Build price list with Code/Item/Price: P11/Paper/75; P12/Ink/340; P13/Folder/25; P14/Stapler/95. On Orders sheet enter P12 qty 3, P11 qty 6, P14 qty 2, P13 qty 10. Use XLOOKUP or VLOOKUP to retrieve item/price; calculate line total; validate codes against the price list; show grand total.
hint: Check one code manually, then test an invalid code.
check: The total should be R1,910. Check that changing an item code changes the lookup results and that an invalid code is rejected.
alignment: 2022 Q9–10; 2023 Q9; 2024/2025 Q9 and later spreadsheet tasks; 2020 Section C

title: College information campaign
prompt: Use Excel to analyse 4 workshop attendance values (Mon 26, Tue 34, Wed 41, Thu 39) and create a chart. Insert the chart into a one-page Word report with two evidence-based conclusions. Create a OneNote page with a summary and checklist. Save original files and export one-page evidence for each application.
hint: Finish the workbook first so your written conclusions match the numbers.
check: Attendance adds to 140. Wednesday was highest at 41. Confirm that the Word conclusions match the Excel chart and that OneNote has both a summary and checklist.
alignment: 2020 alternative practical sections; 2022–2025 combined practical workflow

title: Timed examination simulation
prompt: Within 75 minutes complete: (A) a professional email explaining why a suspicious attachment should not be opened (10); (B) a Word invitation with a two-column schedule table and header (20); (C) Excel expense table with 4 amounts R450, R780, R320, R650, 15% VAT, total and chart (20); (D) OneNote notebook with a section, page and formatted checklist (10). Submit editable files.
hint: Allocate the 75 minutes by section and reserve final minutes for file checks.
check: Check the email, Word, Excel and OneNote evidence separately. Excel subtotal R2,200, VAT R330 and final total R2,530. Open each editable file before submission.
alignment: 2020 alternative practical sections; 2022–2025 combined practical workflow
